newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch mull extra ECOFIN before Amsterdam summit.
newsitem.headline: Dutch mull extra ECOFIN before Amsterdam summit.

text.p: The Dutch EU presidency said on Tuesday it had no immediate plans to hold an extra session of European Union finance ministers (ECOFIN) ahead of Monday's Amsterdam summit, but could not rule one out.

"It's not sure yet that we have an extra gathering...that depends whether there is any substance to decide on. I think a decision will be taken at the end of this week," a Dutch finance ministry spokesman in The Hague told Reuters.

"It will be a last-minute decision, but I would not be surprised if we come up with a Dublin formula," he added, referring to last December's eve-of-summit meeting of finance ministers to pave the way for agreement in Dublin on a stability pact as part of planned monetary union.
The spokesman said the Dutch would wait and see what emerged from two meetings in France this week before deciding whether a special session would be needed.

European Commission president Jacques Santer visits President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Lionel Jospin in Paris on Thursday, while Franco-German leaders are due to meet in Poitiers in western France on Friday.

The need for a special meeting before EU leaders gather in Amsterdam has been highlighted by Jospin's demands for more time to review the bloc's budget stability pact, which was supposed to have been approved at next week's summit.
